steps.title: Hits that look like hits
steps.body: How a body reacts depends on how it was hit: a light hit flinches, a hard one staggers, a charge, a drop or a bomb knocks it down, fire sets it hopping and patting out the flames, ice freezes it stiff, a beam jolts it, a stun leaves it dizzy. The hero, neighbours and enemies all react this way. Here you make a howler that a heavy swing knocks flat. First, place a Howler from the Starter pack.

steps.title: Read about PackHunter
steps.body: In Logic, under Built-in › Brains, press PackHunter. Under Hooks from EnemyBrain: hurtReaction(e) → a name. e.how is the reaction the hit makes; return another to react that way.

steps.title: A glass jaw
steps.body: Press Extend and write hurtReaction: a hit that would stagger it knocks it down instead (and says so); every other hit reacts as the engine says (super).

steps.title: Give it to the Howler
steps.body: In Characters, the Howler's Behaviour tab: + Script → My PackHunter.
steps.task: Attach My PackHunter to the Howler.

steps.title: Hit it hard
steps.body: Press Play, walk up to the Howler and swing hard (hold Shift and press F). It is knocked flat, rolls onto its side and gets up again; the Console says Down it goes! A light swing (F) only makes it flinch.
steps.task: Press Play and give the Howler a heavy hit.

steps.title: Done!
steps.body: Every body reacts by the hit: Cinderjaw's charge and Threadback's drop knock the hero down (it can't move until it gets up), a breath of fire sets it burning, Watcher Eye's beam jolts it, a Flitterwing of ice freezes it. hurtReaction is on the Hero and Damageable too, and the React to a hit card (react(who, how)) makes anyone react without being hurt: a trap, a cutscene's blow.
